Sized 43 x 55 mm or 1016 × 1300 pixels, it must have a plain white background, no frames or digital enhancements, and follow a few other essential specifications. Our complete 2026 UAE visa photo requirements Guide covers them all, so you can create a technically compliant, application-ready photo. Residence applicants can prepare an Emirates ID residence visa photo on its own page. Source: ICP 11 Essential UAE Visa Photo Requirements: a Checklist Emirates visa photo requirements are determined by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs, and Port Security (ICP). In turn, they follow the biometric standards established by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO). Only official photos that match the 11 specifications listed below are accepted with UAE visa applications. The ICP sets separate specifications for travel documents, collected in our UAE passport photo rules 2026 guide. Requirement Details 1. Recency The photo must be taken within the last six months and accurately reflect the applicant's current appearance. 2. UAE Visa Photo Size Requirements 43x55 mm (1.69×2.17 inches), with the face size measuring between 31 and 44 mm (1.2-1.7 inches) , or approximately 70-80% of the image height. 3. Color The image must be in color and accurately reflect the applicant's natural skin tone and hair color. 4. Background Plain white background with no shadows, patterns, or objects visible in the frame. 5. Lighting Even, uniform lighting . No shadows or reflections can be present in the image, neither on the applicant's face nor in the background. 6. Positioning and Framing The applicant must face the camera directly , with head and shoulders square to the camera. No borders or margins are allowed. 7. Facial Expression A neutral facial expression is required for visa and passport applications — eyes open, mouth closed. No smiling, frowning, or any other exaggerated facial expressions are allowed. 8. Attire, Head Covering, and Accessories Regular clothes that don't blend with the background are required. Military or camouflage wear isn't allowed. Religious attire worn daily is acceptable if it doesn't obstruct the face or hairline. Head coverings are allowed only if worn for religious or medical reasons. 9. Glasses Prescription glasses are allowed on United Arab Emirates visa photos . The applicant's eyes must remain fully visible: no flash reflection or glare can be present. Tinted glasses, including sunglasses and prescription lenses, aren't acceptable. If an applicant is wearing glasses for medical reasons, for example, after surgery, a statement from the doctor must be included with the application. 10. UAE Visa Digital Photo Requirements The image should be high resolution, in focus, sharp, and compression-free. Resolution: at least 600 DPI (1016×1300 pixels), file size between 1 MB and 15 MB, accepted formats: JPG, JPEG, PNG . 11. Print Quality Photos must be professionally printed on photographic matte or glossy paper . No frames or decorations are allowed. The image must be sharp, free from pixelation, over- or under-exposure, or any other marks. Acceptable UAE Visa Photo Examples Unacceptable UAE Visa Photo Examples Digital vs Paper Emirates Visa Photo Explained Digital photos are required for online Emirates/Dubai visa photo submissions . The image must be saved as a JPG, JPEG, or PNG file between 1 MB and 15 MB, and have the dimensions of at least 1016×1300 pixels. Printed photos are required for in-person UAE visa submissions through Emirati consulates, embassies, or authorised agents. Only photos, professionally printed on high-quality photographic paper, either matte or glossy, are accepted. The photo size is 43x55 mm (1.69×2.17 inches), with the face size 31-44 mm (1.2-1.7 inches). To qualify, the sponsor must earn at least AED 4,000 per month (or AED 3,000 with company housing) and prove the relationship with attested marriage or birth certificates. UAE dependent visa photo requirements are identical to those for all other applicants: The image must be 43 × 55 mm with a plain white background and no shadows. The dependent’s face should fill 70-80% of the frame, looking directly at the camera with a neutral expression, eyes open, and mouth closed. Head coverings are only allowed for daily religious wear that doesn’t obscure the face. Glasses are permitted only if the eyes remain fully visible without glare; tinted lenses are prohibited. The photo must be taken within the last six months and printed on high-quality photo paper without any digital retouching. What are the UAE Visa Photo Requirements for Children and Babies? UAE visa photos for children must follow specific rules so that the image can be used for biometric identification. A child must be photographed alone, facing the camera, with a neutral background and no distracting objects in view. The picture must be sharp, in color, and evenly lit, free of strong shadows, glare, or reflections on the face or in the background. Infants and Babies Under 1 Newborns and very young babies are photographed lying down, on a plain, light-colored surface such as a sheet or blanket. The camera should be positioned directly above — the baby’s face is clearly visible and centered in the frame. For this age group, it is generally acceptable that the eyes may not fully open or the mouth can be slightly open, provided the facial features are clear and recognisable. Toddlers and Young Children (Ages 1 to 5) For toddlers and preschool-age children, the main requirement for a UAE visa photo is that the face is visible and unobstructed. A perfectly neutral expression can be difficult to achieve at this age, so a natural, relaxed look is usually acceptable as long as the child is facing the camera. No toys, pacifiers, furniture, or adults should appear in the image, and the background must remain plain. Older Children (Ages 6 to 15) Older children are expected to follow the same UAE visa photo standards as adults. They should sit or stand upright, look directly into the camera, and maintain a calm, neutral expression with their mouth closed. The eyes must be open and clearly visible, and the entire head and upper shoulders should be within the frame. Expression Neutral facial expression, no crying or laughing. Frame No toys, parents’ hands, or other objects in the frame. 8 Common Reasons for an UAE Visa Photo Rejection Below is a list of the most common reasons behind an UAE visa photo rejection. Wrong photo size . Even the slightest difference in the UAE visa photo size can cause rejection by authorities. The exact size is 43x55 mm, with the head taking 70-80% of the shot. Incorrect framing . Your UAE visa photo will be rejected if the head is tilted or not centred in the frame. You must look straight at the camera, with head and shoulders fully visible. Non‑white background . A UAE visa photo is refused if the background is not plain white. Any colour tint, pattern, texture, or shadows behind the applicant count as a defect. Exaggerated facial expressions . If the applicant is smiling, frowning, or showing any other exaggerated expressions, a visa photo won’t be accepted. Glasses blocking the eyes . A visa photo will not be accepted if the glasses hide the eyes. Glare on lenses, thick frames covering the eyes, tinted lenses, or sunglasses are common reasons for rejection. Obstructed facial features . The photo will be refused if headwear or accessories obscure facial features. Poor image quality . Blurred focus, noise, strong filters, over‑ or under‑exposure, or heavy shadows are typical grounds for refusal. Wrong digital dimensions . If the image has a resolution lower than 600 DPI (about 1016×1300 pixels), the file size is outside the 1-15 MB range, or the file is provided in a format other than JPG, JPEG, or PNG format, it will not be accepted. Who Needs a UAE Visa and How to Apply For a short-term stay, most foreigners either enter the UAE visa‑free with a visa on arrival. If your nationality is not eligible for visa‑free entry, or you plan to stay in the Emirates for an extended period, you must obtain a visit or tourist visa before travelling. You can apply for a UAE visit visa through several official channels: UAE government e‑portal ICP Smart Services Registered travel agencies and tour operators that submit applications via approved UAE partners UAE missions abroad — embassies and consulates Required Documents for a Dubai Visit Visa According to the ICP official website, the following documents are required for obtaining a UAE visa: Passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry Technically compliant biometric passport-size photo Valid health insurance policy with coverage within the UAE Confirmed return or onward travel ticket If a UAE resident is sponsoring the trip : the minimum monthly salary is AED 4,000 for first‑degree relatives, AED 8,000 for second‑ and third‑degree relatives, and AED 15,000 for friends, plus proof of kinship for sponsored family members according to the degree of relationship Frequently Asked Questions What Size and Dimensions are Required for UAE Visa Photos to Avoid Rejection? To avoid rejection, provide the UAE visa photo in the following formats: For in-person submissions , the required size is 43 x 55 mm (1.69 × 2.17 inches). The head must cover 70-80% of the image. For online applications , you must provide a photo sized 1016 × 1300 pixels in JPG, JPEG, or PNG format and file size from 1 to 15 MB. What are the Current UAE Visa Photo Requirements for a Successful Application? Here is a list of the 2026 Requirements for UAE visa photos: Recency : Taken within the last 6 months. Size : 43×55 mm; face 31-44 mm (70-80% of image height). Color : Color photo; natural skin/hair tones. Background : Plain white; no shadows, patterns, or objects. Lighting : Even lighting; no shadows or glare. Positioning & framing : Straight to camera; head and shoulders square in the shot; no borders/margins. Facial expression : Neutral; eyes open; mouth closed. Attire/head covering/accessories: Normal clothing; no military or camouflage; only religious/medical head coverings are allowed if they don’t obstruct the face and hairline. Glasses: Allowed if eyes are visible, lenses are free from glare; tinted lenses and sunglasses aren’t acceptable. Digital requirements : Sharp, high-resolution of 600 DPI (1016×1300 px); 1-15 MB; JPG/JPEG/PNG. Print quality : High-quality print on photo paper; no visible pixels, blur, banding, stains, or compression artifacts. What are the Background Color and Lighting Requirements for UAE Visa Photos? The background must be light-colored, white, or off-white; plain, free from patterns, textures, or shadows. What Are the UAE Golden Visa Photo Requirements? UAE golden visa photo requirements follow the same rules set by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs, and Port Security (ICP) for all other visa categories: The photograph must measure 43 × 55 mm with a plain white background covering the entire frame. The face must occupy 70-80% of the image (31-44 mm from chin to crown), centered and looking directly at the camera with a neutral expression—mouth closed, eyes open, no smiling. The image must be taken within the last six months, printed in high resolution on photo-quality paper without pixelation or compression artifacts. Head coverings are permitted only for daily religious attire that does not shadow the face. Tinted glasses and sunglasses are prohibited, while prescription glasses are allowed only if the eyes remain fully visible without glare on the lens. Where Can I get UAE Visa Photos Taken That Meet All Official Requirements Near Me? You can get UAE visa photos that meet all official requirements at a professional passport/visa photo studio, a photo counter in a print shop, or a dedicated kiosk in a mall. Your UAE visa photo must have a plain white background, sharp focus, in color. Keep a neutral expression, eyes open, and mouth closed when the photo is being taken. For in-person submissions, ask for a UAE visa photo 43 × 55 mm (4.3 × 5.5 cm) Request a digital file sized 1016×1300 pixels, in high resolution of 600 DPI, saved as a JPG/JPEG/PNG file of 1-15 MB if you’re submitting your Emirates visa application online. What are the UAE Visa Photo Rules for Head Position, Facial Expression, and Eyeglasses? Head position : takes 70-80% of the image, centered in the shot, straight, no tilting allowed. Facial expression : Neutral. No smiling, grinning, frowning, or demonstrating any other exaggerated expressions is allowed. Eyeglasses . Glasses are allowed in the UAE visa photo, but only if the frames don’t obstruct the eyes and the lenses are free from glare and flash reflection. How Can I Take a Compliant UAE Visa Photo at Home That Meets All Specifications? To take a compliant UAE visa photo at home that meets all specifications, you need a smartphone, a simple setup, and an online passport photo maker like PhotoGov. Follow these simple steps: Arrange a simple setup. Take your photo in the daytime. Choose a well-lit spot, preferably by the window. If the walls in the place where you’re taking the photo aren’t white or off-white, hang a sheet of white paper or a sheet of white fabric on the wall. Use a tripod or ask someone to take your photo . The picture should be taken from a distance of about 1 meter (40 inches). If you’re taking a selfie, hold the phone steadily 50 cm (20 inches) away from your face. Take a few shots and choose the sharpest one. Upload a photo to PhotoGov . Wait about 30 seconds while the platform automatically converts it into a UAE visa photo that meets all specifications. Download your Emirates visa photo . You can choose a digital file for online submissions or a printable PDF file for in-person submissions. Simply upload your selfie to our platform, and it will be converted into an ICP-compliant, application-ready photo in less than 30 seconds. All official Emirates visa photo requirements are applied automatically, and technical compliance of the photo is guaranteed. What Can I Wear for the Dubai Visa Photo? Wear your daily clothes, trying to avoid bright, neon colors and big lettering. Military wear isn't accepted at official photographs. Attire worn for religious reasons that doesn't cover the face or the hairline is acceptable for UAE passport or visa pictures. Can I Smile in UAE Visa Photo? No. Smiling, frowning, or demonstrating any other exaggerated expressions isn’t allowed in UAE visa photos. Are Picture Sizes the Same for UAE Visa, ID, and Passport? No. In the Emirates, the official visa photograph size is 43x55 mm, while ID Card photograph dimensions are 35x40 mm, and passport-size is 45x55 mm. Frequently Asked Questions Planning a trip and wondering what the Saudi Arabia eVisa photo requirements are in 2026? You must submit one digital photo with a white background at 200 × 200 pixels, file size 5–100 KB, and face taking up 70–80% of the photo (1.4" × 1.6" from chin to crown). The photo must be taken within the past 6 months and submitted online via an eVisa portal. You can produce a Saudi e visa photo 200x200 px from an ordinary selfie with our online maker. This guide covers all current eVisa photo specifications directly from the official Tourism Website of Saudi Arabia , provides eVisa photo samples, and offers practical tips to help you create an accurate image and avoid application delays or rejections. Residents applying for an Iqama or national ID need a Saudi Arabia ID card photo in the 4 x 6 cm format instead. 10 Essential Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Requirements Saudi Arabia Ministry of Tourism sets the official eVisa specifications, based on the international biometric standards of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Document 9303 . The photo you submit with your eVisa application must follow all 10 specs listed below to avoid delays or rejections. Parameter Requirement 1. Number of photos One identical digital photograph per applicant. 2. Recency Must be no more than six months old to reflect an applicant’s up-to-date likeness. 3. Size 200 × 200 pixels , square (1:1). 4. Head size 1.4 × 1.6 in from chin to crown, or 70-80% of the shot. 5. File size 5 to 100 KB. 6. Framing Close-up of the face and top of the shoulders, square in the shot. 7. Background White , plain, with no pattern and no shadows. 8. Facial expression Only a neutral facial expression is allowed. 9. Head covering Not permitted, except for religious or medical reasons. When worn, the face must remain visible from the lower chin to the forehead, with no shadow cast on the face. 10. Eyewear Preferably removed . If you must wear glasses for medical reasons, make sure that the lenses have zero glare, no tinting, and both eyes fully visible. Saudi eVisa Photos: Special Cases Head Coverings Headwear is generally not permitted, except for religious head coverings such as hijabs, keffiyehs, and turbans, which are explicitly allowed under official guidance. In these cases, the face must remain fully visible from the chin to the forehead, and the fabric must not cast any shadow across the face. Medical Head Coverings Medical head coverings fall under the same exception category as religious ones, subject to the identical visibility standard: full chin-to-forehead exposure with no shadowing from the covering. Voluminous or Textured Hair For applicants with voluminous or textured hair, the specification requires that the head and hairstyle be shown in full — the photo should not be cropped tightly just to accommodate hair volume. The face-size requirement takes precedence over fitting the entire hairstyle into a tighter frame. Eyewear Remove glasses entirely for the photo. If they must be worn for medical reasons, the frame must not cross the eyes, and there should be no glare or tinting on the lenses. Step-by-Step: How to Upload Your Photo on visa.visitsaudi.com Step 1. Prepare your photo file at exactly 200 × 200 pixels, between 5 and 100 KB, on a plain white background. Step 2. Create or log in to your account on the eVisa portal and start a new application. Note that the system sends a verification code to your email both at registration and at every subsequent login — you won't be able to access your account without entering it. Step 3. Enter your passport and personal details, then proceed to the photo upload step. Step 4. Upload your photo file. The system automatically checks file size and dimensions; a file outside the 5–100 KB range or not sized 200 × 200 px will be rejected before you can continue. Step 5. Review the preview the portal displays — confirm the face is centered and fills roughly 70–80% of the frame before submitting. Step 6. Complete payment. The portal adds the applicable visa, digital-service, and insurance-related charges. The insurance premium depends on the selected provider, so check the final amount displayed at checkout. Most applications are approved quickly; check your account or email for confirmation and your linked eVisa. How to Apply for a Saudi Arabia Tourist eVisa The entire application process takes place online through the official portal, visa.visitsaudi.com . You'll need a passport valid for at least six months beyond your planned stay, a digital passport-style photo meeting the specifications above, and a valid payment method for the visa fee. The official processing estimate ranges from one minute to three business days. The approved eVisa is sent as an email attachment. Carry a copy of it when arriving in Saudi Arabia. Where to Take a Saudi eVisa Photo (and What It Costs) Choose whichever location is most convenient for you, or simply take the photo at home and process it with a reliable online photo-making tool. Pharmacy photo counters (e.g., CVS, Walgreens) — Widely available and generally familiar with visa-photo formats, but staff often default to producing a standard printed passport photo unless you specifically request a digital file sized to the Saudi eVisa's 200×200-pixel spec. Stand far enough in front of the wall to prevent shadows, and position the camera approximately 1.5–2 meters away at eye level. The natural light coming from the front is preferable to overhead lighting or flash, both of which tend to produce the shadows the specification explicitly prohibits. Position. Face the camera directly with your head square — not turned or tilted — ensuring both ears and cheeks remain visible, in line with the official wording. Camera. Use a smartphone's rear camera rather than the front-facing selfie camera, since it typically offers better resolution and less distortion. A tripod, or having a second person take the shot, produces a straighter, better-centered result than a handheld photo. After the shot. Crop the image to a perfect square (1:1 ratio) and resize it to exactly 200 × 200 pixels, then confirm the file size falls between 5 and 100 KB before uploading. Most basic photo editors and free online tools can handle both steps. Visual Do's and Don'ts Do Don't Plain white background, no shadows Off-white, patterned, or shadowed background Head square to the camera Head turned, tilted, or in profile Face filling 70–80% of the frame Face too small or too tightly cropped Religious/medical headwear with full face visible Caps, hats, or sunglasses worn without religious/medical reason Exactly 200 × 200 px, 5–100 KB Photo sized for a printed passport photo Recent photo (within 6 months) Reused photo from an old application Both ears and cheeks visible Side profile or heavily angled shot Full head and hairstyle shown if hair is voluminous Tightly cropped photo that cuts off hair to fit the frame Saudi eVisa Photo Requirements for Children The photo requirements for children are the same as for adults, with no exceptions for age. Each child must have an individual photo — 200 × 200 pixels, plain white background, 5–100 KB file size — with no other person in the frame. No parent's hands, arms, or body may appear in the shot, even partially, and no toys, pacifiers, or props of any kind are allowed. For infants and toddlers who can't sit or stand independently, laying the child flat on a plain white sheet or blanket and photographing from directly above works well, as long as the background around the face and shoulders stays plain white with no folds or shadows. Why Saudi eVisa Photos Get Rejected — the Most Common Reasons Wrong file dimensions The photo must be exactly 200 × 200 pixels. Photos formatted for a printed passport photo, for example, 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm, do not meet this digital spec and will be rejected. File size outside the 5–100 KB range A high-resolution photo taken straight from a smartphone is almost always too large and needs compressing first. Overcompressing can also cause problems, pushing the file below 5 KB and triggering rejection at the opposite end of the range. Off-white or shadowed background Any tint, gradient, or visible shadow behind the applicant violates the "no pattern, no shadows" rule and is one of the most common reasons for rejection. Head tilted, not square in the shot The specification requires the head to be square to the camera, with both ears and cheeks visible. A side-angled or tilted photo does not meet this standard. Face too small or too large in frame The face must take 70–80% of the frame. This requirement is most often missed by photographing from too far away or by cropping too tightly. Non-religious head covering Hats, caps, or sunglasses worn without a religious or medical reason are rejected under the general rule that headwear is not permitted. Shadow cast by religious headwear Even when a religious head covering itself is allowed, a shadow falling across the face from the fabric can still cause the photo to be rejected. Outdated photo .A photo older than six months, or one that no longer reflects the applicant's current appearance, does not meet the recency requirement. What to Do If Your Saudi eVisa Photo is Rejected Once you've identified which of the issues above caused the rejection, the fix follows the same basic pattern: correct that specific cause, then retake and re-upload the photo. If the problem was dimensions or file size, resize the image to exactly 200 × 200 pixels and adjust compression until it falls within 5–100 KB — don't simply crop or shrink the existing file, since heavy compression often degrades image quality and can trigger a second rejection. If the problem was the background, lighting, or head position, retake the photo entirely against a plain white wall with even, front-facing light, keeping the head square to the camera and both ears visible; a poor original is rarely worth salvaging through editing. If the issue was headwear-related — either a non-permitted item or a shadow from religious head covering — adjust the lighting angle or remove the non-permitted item and take a new photo rather than trying to edit shadows out. Once the corrected photo is ready, upload it through your existing application on the official eVisa portal; there is no separate fee for fixing a photo before final submission. If your eVisa has already been issued and you need a new one for a future trip, you'll need to submit a completely new application, since photos are not carried over between separate applications. The photo is only one requirement — make sure your passport is valid for at least six months from your intended date of entry, your application form is complete, and any supporting documents are ready to upload. Check if other Saudi Arabia documents need a photo too. Frequently Asked Questions What is the Saudi Arabia Tourist eVisa Photo Size? The Saudi Arabia tourist eVisa photo must be exactly 200 × 200 pixels, with a file size between 5 and 100 KB. This is a digital-only specification, so a printed passport-style format such as 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm does not meet the requirement. If the file is too large, it must be compressed; if it is too small, it must be re-saved at a slightly higher quality before upload. What Background is Required for a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo? The background must be plain white, with no pattern, no visible texture, and no shadows behind the applicant. Even a slight tint or a soft gradient can cause the photo to be rejected, so lighting matters as much as the backdrop itself. For the cleanest result, use even front-facing light and avoid flash or overhead lighting. How Recent Must a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Be? The photo must have been taken within the last six months and should reflect the applicant’s current appearance. Older images are a common reason for rejection, especially if the haircut, facial hair, or general appearance has changed. A recent photo also reduces the risk of the upload being flagged as outdated during review. What Head Size is Required for a Saudi Arabia eVisa? The face should occupy 70–80% of the image, measured from the chin to the crown. In practice, this means the photo should be a close-up of the face and upper shoulders, not a full bust shot and not an overly tight crop. If the face is too small, the image looks distant; if it is too large, the head may be cut off, or the framing may fail the specification. What Facial Expression is Required for a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo? The expression must be neutral, with the face looking directly at the camera. Smiling broadly, opening the mouth, or making an exaggerated expression can lead to rejection because the photo must show a natural, standard passport-style likeness. The safest approach is a relaxed face with a closed mouth and open eyes. Can I Wear Glasses in a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo? Glasses are best removed unless they are medically necessary. The official rules focus on clear visibility of the face, and glasses can create glare, reflections, or partial eye obstruction, which may lead to rejection. If glasses must remain on, the lenses should be completely clear with both eyes fully visible, and the frame should not cover the eyes. Can I Wear a Hijab or Other Religious Head Covering in a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo? Yes. Religious head coverings are allowed as an explicit exception to the general no-headwear rule. The face still has to remain fully visible from chin to forehead, and the fabric must not cast any shadow across the face. The same principle applies to medical head coverings. Can I Wear Non-Religious Headwear in a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo? No. Hats, caps, fashion headwear, and sunglasses are not permitted unless the covering is worn for religious or medical reasons. Even then, the face must stay fully visible, and the covering must not interfere with the lighting or framing. If there is any doubt, the safest choice is to remove it. Is the Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Digital or Printed? The tourist eVisa uses a digital upload only. The image is submitted through the online application system, and no printed photo is required for the standard tourist route. That means the file must meet both the visual requirements and the technical file-size and pixel-dimension rules before submission. Can I Use a Printed Passport-Style Photo for a Saudi Arabia eVisa? No. Printed passport formats such as 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm are not the same as the eVisa’s digital requirement. The portal is designed for uploading a digital file, so an image prepared for a print workflow will need to be properly resized and reformatted first. You can use PhotoGov to create an eVisa-ready photo in under a minute. What Happens if a Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo File is Outside the 5–100 KB Range? The upload will fail, and the file will need to be corrected before it can be submitted. A smartphone image straight from the camera is often too large, while an overcompressed image can fall below the minimum size. The safest fix is to adjust the file properly before re-uploading, rather than trying to force an incorrect file through the portal. What Rules Apply to Infant Saudi Arabia eVisa Photos? Infants must still be photographed alone, with no other people, hands, toys, or props visible in the frame. The image should show the child clearly against a plain white background, with the face centered and lighting kept even. If the child cannot sit upright, a flat white surface can be used as long as the final image remains clean and compliant. Do I Need a New Saudi eVisa Photo for Every Trip? No. A Saudi tourist eVisa is normally valid for one year and permits multiple entries, unless otherwise stated on the issued visa. You do not need to submit a new application or photo for each trip while the eVisa and the passport used for the application remain valid. Always check the validity and entry conditions shown on your issued eVisa. How Should a Rejected Saudi Arabia eVisa Photo Be Fixed? Identify the exact issue that caused the rejection, then correct it and upload a new file through the same application. If the problem is technical, such as size or dimensions, resize and re-save the image; if the problem is visual, such as lighting, framing, or headwear, retake the photo. The best results usually come from starting with a fresh image rather than trying to rescue a flawed one. Whether you are a South African expat moving for work or renewing your status, having an incorrect photo is the reason for application rejection. The Ministry of Interior (MOI) maintains strict digital standards for the Qatar ID (QID) . In this ultimate guide, we reveal the hidden mistakes travelers make and provide the complete specifications to ensure your document is approved on the first try. Conclusion Farhana Oberson Official Qatar ID Photo Requirements 2026 To meet the Qatar ID Photo Requirements , your image must be high-resolution and taken within the last six months. The government uses biometric face-recognition software, so clarity is non-negotiable. Technical Specifications Dimensions: 38 mm (width) x 48 mm (height). Resolution: 300 to 600 DPI (Dots Per Inch). Background: Plain white (must be clean with no shadows). Face Coverage: Your face must cover 70-80% of the frame. Head Size: 32–36 mm from the chin to the top of the head. Format: Digital files for online submission should be roughly 450×570 pixels. Lighting and Quality The photo must be in color . Black and white photos are strictly prohibited. Ensure there are no “red-eye” effects or harsh shadows behind the ears or under the chin. Qatar ID vs. Qatar Visa Photo Requirements Many South Africans confuse the Qatar work visa photo with the ID requirements. While they are similar, the background color can sometimes vary based on the specific visa type (e.g., A1 visas vs. Work Residencies). Feature Qatar ID (QID) Qatar Visa (General) Background Color Plain White White (Standard) / Blue (Occasional) Dimensions 38×48 mm 35×45 mm or 40×60 mm Expression Neutral Only Neutral Only Digital Check Required via Metrash2 Required via MOI Portal Expert Tip: While some older sources mention a Qatar visa photo blue background , the current 2026 standard for most official digital residencies is a clean white background . Step-by-Step Guide to Taking the Perfect QID Photo Following these steps will ensure your Qatar ID Photo Requirements are met without a “hidden” error. Find the Right Setting: Use a professional studio or a wall with a flat white finish. Avoid “off-white” or cream colors. Position the Camera: The camera should be at eye level. Looking up or down distorts the facial geometry used for biometrics. Check Your Expression: Keep your mouth closed and eyes wide open. Do not smile or frown. Manage Your Attire: Wear everyday clothing. Avoid uniforms or white clothing that blends into the background. Digital Export: If uploading to the Ministry of Interior (MOI) Qatar portal , ensure the file size is under the maximum MB limit specified on the form. Rules for Glasses, Hijabs, and Facial Hair Head Coverings Head coverings are only allowed for religious reasons (such as the Hijab or Turban). Even then, the face must be fully visible from the bottom of the chin to the top of the forehead. Eyeglasses Glasses are generally not recommended . If you must wear them for medical reasons, they must not have tinted lenses or create a glare. The frames must not cover any part of your eyes. Facial Hair If you normally have a beard, you may keep it. However, it is essential that your facial features remain distinguishable. What Happens if Photo is Rejected? If your Qatar ID photo is rejected, the Ministry of Interior Qatar will notify you through the MOI portal or Metrash app and request a new photo meeting official biometric standards. How Long Does Qatar ID Photo Approval Take? According to Ministry of Interior Qatar, Qatar ID photo approval usually takes 1 to 3 working days after submission through the official MOI portal or Metrash app. The system checks biometric standards, image quality, and size requirements. If your photo does not meet specifications or application volume is high, processing may take up to 5 working days . Applicants should regularly check their application status through official MOI services for updates. Can I Update Qatar ID Photo Online? According to Ministry of Interior Qatar services, you generally cannot update your Qatar ID photo fully online . Most photo updates require visiting an official Government Services Center with a new photo that meets biometric requirements. However, in some cases, limited requests or document updates may be submitted through the Metrash app or MOI services, but final verification often requires physical processing. Always follow official MOI instructions to avoid application delays. MOI Photo Upload Error Solutions According to Ministry of Interior Qatar guidelines, MOI photo upload errors usually occur due to incorrect image size, wrong format, low resolution, or background issues. The system automatically checks biometric standards before accepting the photo. To fix MOI upload errors: Ensure the photo size meets official requirements (38×48 mm, correct pixels). Use a plain white background with no shadows. Upload high-resolution images (300–600 DPI). Save the file in JPEG or PNG format within the allowed size limit. Clear browser cache or retry using the official MOI portal or Metrash app. If the error continues, visit an official Government Services Center for assistance to avoid delays in your application process. Common Mistakes To Avoid For Qatar ID Photos Understanding Qatar ID Photo Requirements also means knowing what not to do. Avoid these shocking mistakes that delay thousands of applications: The “Selfie” Error: Selfies are never accepted. The lens distortion from a front-facing phone camera changes your facial proportions. Old Photos: Using a photo older than 6 months. If you have significantly changed your appearance (weight loss, hair color), take a new one. Shadows: Shadows on the background or one side of the face are the most common cause for digital “Checker” tools to fail. Busy Backgrounds: Using a background with patterns or objects. Benefits & Drawbacks of DIY Photos Benefits of Using a Professional Guaranteed compliance with Qatar ID Photo Requirements . Proper lighting setup to avoid shadows. High-end equipment for 600 DPI resolution. Drawbacks of DIY (At Home) High Risk: Small errors in mm size can lead to rejection. DPI Issues: Most home printers or basic phone apps do not reach the required 300–600 DPI quality. Wasted Time: A rejected photo can delay your QID by weeks. FAQs About Qatar ID Photos 1. How can I change my Qatar ID photo? You can change your QID photo by visiting a Government Services Center. You must provide a new physical photo that meets the current specifications and pay a small replacement fee. 2. Is there a Qatar visa photo checker online? Yes, the MOI and various [internal link placeholder: Visa Assistance Portals] offer digital validation tools that check for resolution and face-to-frame ratios. 3. What is the Qatar visa photo size free download format? For most digital applications, you should save your photo as a JPEG or PNG file with a width of 38mm and height of 48mm at 300 DPI. 4. Can I wear a white shirt for my Qatar ID photo? It is strongly discouraged to wear a white shirt because it blends into the white background, making the edges of your shoulders invisible to the biometric scanner. 5. What are the Qatar a1 visa photo requirements? The A1 visa usually follows the standard 38x48mm rule with a white background, though always check your specific sponsor’s latest update. Conclusion Adhering to the Qatar ID Photo Requirements is the easiest way to ensure your residency process in Qatar is smooth and stress-free. Use a professional We recommend you have your photo taken by a professional passport photograph provider and have a digital copy of the photo emailed to you. We recommend the Australian Post Office . Or use a similar provider if you are applying from outside Australia. We don’t recommend using online passport photo services and mobile apps as images produced may not meet our image quality requirements. Also, you may be in danger of identity fraud. How to provide a suitable photo Photo quality The photo must: be no more than 6 months old show your full face ​be of good quality, in colour, taken against a neutral or light grey coloured background that contrasts with your face be unedited (do not remove background, moles, wrinkles, scars or red eyes) have a clear, focused image with no marks or 'red eye' have uniform lighting (no shadows or reflections), with appropriate brightness and contrast to show natural skin tone have no brighter or darker areas of the face caused by lighting or exposure. Your full-face view Ensure your: face is centred and looking at the camera straight on; not tilted in any direction hair is off your face, so that the edges of your face are visible eyes are open and mouth is closed expression is neutral (not smiling, laughing or frowning). Glasses must be removed If you cannot remove your glasses for medical reasons, they should be untinted (except for medical reasons). The frames can’t obscure your eyes and there can’t be any reflection from the lenses. Vision impairment alone is not an acceptable reason to wear glasses in a citizenship photo. Head coverings If you wear a head covering for religious reasons, you can wear it in your photo. Religious head coverings have to be worn in a way that shows your whole face from the bottom of the chin to the top of the forehead (it must not cover any features of the face).  The edges of your face on either side also have to be visible (including the outer eye corner). Coverings must be plain material without any patterns. Jewellery must not obscure Jewellery can’t obscure any part of your face, especially the area around your eyes, mouth and nose. There can’t be any reflection from nose rings or studs. Babies and infants For infants (under 3 years of age), a photo with an open mouth is acceptable. The photo has to comply with all the other requirements. No other person or object can be visible in the photo. Online applications If applying online the photo should be in digital JPEG format between 70 Kb and 3.5 Mb. The preferred resolution is 1200 x 1600 pixels. A scan of a photo or a photograph of a photo is not acceptable. Paper applications If applying on paper the photo should be passport-sized: 35 mm to 40 mm wide and 45 mm to 50 mm high. The size of the face from chin to crown can be up to a maximum of 36 mm, with a minimum of 32 mm. A blurry image, the wrong background color, or a file that’s too large can delay your travel plans by days. And if you’re applying close to your departure date, that’s time you don’t have to waste. The good news is that getting your photo right is straightforward once you know the exact specifications. This guide covers everything you need to know, based on the official Thai e-Visa photo requirements . What Is the Thai e-Visa? The Thai e-Visa is an online visa application system that allows eligible travelers to apply for permission to enter Thailand without visiting an embassy in person. It covers several visa categories, including tourist visas, non-immigrant visas, and transit visas. Who Needs to Apply Online? Nationals from eligible countries can submit their application, supporting documents, and visa fee entirely online through the official Thai e-Visa portal . The system was introduced to make the process faster and more accessible for international travelers. Why Photo Quality Matters for Approval Your photo is one of the first things visa officers review. If it doesn’t meet the required specifications, your application will be flagged for rejection — even if every other document is perfect. Unlike paper applications where you can resubmit quickly, errors in an online application may require you to start the process again. Getting the photo right the first time saves you time, money, and stress. Official Thai e-Visa Photo Specifications Quick Reference: A Thai e-Visa photo must be in JPG or JPEG format, sized between 200 KB and 2 MB, with dimensions of at least 350 x 450 pixels, shot against a plain white background, and showing a clear, front-facing view of the applicant’s full face. Here is a full breakdown of the required specifications: Specification Requirement File Format JPG / JPEG only Minimum Dimensions 350 x 450 pixels (width x height) Recommended Dimensions 600 x 800 pixels or higher File Size Between 200 KB and 2 MB Resolution Minimum 300 DPI recommended Background Color Plain white only Face Coverage 70–80% of the frame Photo Age Taken within the last 6 months Required Photo Dimensions Your photo must be at least 350 x 450 pixels (width x height). Royal Thai Embassy recommends submitting a higher resolution image — ideally 600 x 800 pixels — to ensure the image is sharp and clear when reviewed by immigration officers. Do not submit a cropped screenshot or a photo scanned at low resolution. These commonly fail the automated image check. Accepted File Formats Only JPG or JPEG files are accepted. PNG, PDF, HEIC, and other formats will be rejected by the system. If your phone saves photos in HEIC format (common on iPhones), you will need to convert the file before uploading. Maximum and Minimum File Size The photo file must be between 200 KB and 2 MB . Files smaller than 200 KB are often low quality and will be rejected. Files larger than 2 MB will not upload successfully on the portal. If your photo is too large, use a free image compression tool to reduce the file size without significantly lowering quality. Resolution Requirements A minimum of 300 DPI is recommended for a clear, printable-quality image. Photos taken on a modern smartphone in good lighting typically meet this standard automatically. Photo Composition Guidelines The technical specifications are only part of the picture. The composition — how your face appears in the photo — is equally important. Background Color Requirements The background must be plain white . No patterns, textures, gradients, or off-white shades are acceptable. Gray, cream, or light blue backgrounds that look white on-screen may still be rejected. If you are taking the photo at home, stand against a white wall in a well-lit room. Avoid casting shadows on the background. Facial Expression and Head Position Look directly into the camera with both eyes fully open Keep a neutral expression — no smiling with teeth, no frowning Your head must be straight , not tilted to either side Both ears should be visible Your full face from chin to the top of your head must be in the frame Lighting and Shadow Rules Use even, natural lighting — avoid harsh flash that washes out your face There should be no shadows on your face or the background Avoid backlighting (do not stand in front of a window) Glasses, Headwear, and Accessories Glasses are not permitted in Thai e-Visa photos, in line with ICAO biometric photo standards Headwear is not permitted unless worn for documented religious reasons Hair should not cover the face or obscure the facial features No heavy filters or editing — the photo must be a true representation of your appearance How to Take or Prepare a Compliant Thai e-Visa Photo Taking the Photo at Home You can take a compliant photo at home with a smartphone. Follow these steps: Find a plain white wall with good natural light Position yourself 1–2 feet from the wall to avoid background shadows Ask someone to hold the phone at eye level , or use a tripod Wear everyday clothing — avoid white tops that blend into the background Remove glasses and any non-religious headwear Take several shots and choose the clearest, most evenly lit one Check that your face fills 70–80% of the frame before uploading Using a Professional Photographer Many passport photo services are familiar with e-Visa requirements. Ask specifically for a digital passport-style photo on a white background in JPG format. Confirm they can provide the file digitally at the required resolution and file size. Online Tools to Resize and Format Your Photo If your photo doesn’t quite meet the size or format requirements, several free online tools can help: Compress the file size: Tools like Squoosh or TinyJPG can reduce file size without major quality loss Resize dimensions: Use Adobe Express, Canva, or a simple photo editor to adjust pixel dimensions Convert HEIC to JPG: Use iLoveIMG or your phone’s built-in export settings Always double-check the final file before uploading — confirm the format, size, and dimensions are within the accepted range. Common Photo Mistakes That Lead to Rejection These are the most frequent reasons Thai e-Visa photos are rejected, based on guidance from Royal Thai Embassy : Incorrect File Size or Dimensions Uploading a photo under 200 KB or over 2 MB will cause an immediate upload failure. Similarly, photos significantly smaller than 350 x 450 pixels may be rejected for poor quality. Fix: Check your file size and dimensions before uploading. Most computers show this information when you right-click the file and view its properties. Poor Lighting or Blurry Image A dark, shadowy, or out-of-focus photo will be rejected. This is one of the most common issues with self-taken photos. Fix: Take the photo in a bright room near a window, but avoid direct sunlight. Use the rear camera on your phone rather than the front-facing camera, which typically has lower resolution. Non-White Background A cream, light gray, or patterned background — even one that looks white on your phone screen — will fail the review. Fix: Use a pure white background only. If needed, some photo editing tools allow background removal and replacement with a white fill, but the result must look natural. Wearing Glasses or Unauthorized Headwear This is a straightforward reason for rejection that is easy to avoid. Fix: Remove glasses before taking your photo. If you wear headwear for religious reasons, check the official Thai e-Visa portal for the documentation required to support this. Step-by-Step: Uploading Your Photo to the Thai e-Visa Portal Where to Upload When completing your Thai e-Visa application at the official Thai e-Visa portal (royalthaiembassy.com), you will reach a section that asks you to upload your personal photo. This is separate from the document upload section. Click the upload button, locate your photo file on your device, and select it. The system will run an automated check on the file format and size before accepting it. What Happens After Submission Once your photo passes the initial system check, it will be reviewed by a visa officer alongside your other documents. If there is a problem with the photo that was not caught automatically, you may receive a request to resubmit. Check your email regularly after submitting your application. For guidance on starting your application, visit https://royalthaiembassy.com/ . Frequently Asked Questions What file format is accepted for a Thai e-Visa photo? Only JPG or JPEG files are accepted. PNG, PDF, HEIC, and other formats will be rejected. If your phone saves images in HEIC format, convert the file to JPG before uploading. What background color is required for a Thai e-Visa photo? The background must be plain white. No patterns, off-white shades, or colored backgrounds are accepted. Gray and cream backgrounds are frequently rejected even when they appear white on-screen. Can I wear glasses in my Thai e-Visa photo? No. Glasses are not permitted in Thai e-Visa photos, in line with international biometric photo standards. Remove glasses before taking your photo. How do I reduce my photo file size for the Thai e-Visa upload? Use a free online image compression tool such as Squoosh, TinyJPG, or iLoveIMG. These tools reduce file size without major quality loss. Your final file must be between 200 KB and 2 MB. What should I do if my Thai e-Visa photo is rejected? If your photo is rejected, review the specific reason provided by the portal or in the rejection notification. Retake or reformat your photo to meet the stated requirements, then resubmit. If you are unsure, contact Royal Thai Embassy for clarification before reapplying. Final Tips Before You Submit Before you click submit on your Thai e-Visa application , run through this checklist: File format is JPG or JPEG File size is between 200 KB and 2 MB Dimensions are at least 350 x 450 pixels Background is plain white Face is centered and fills 70–80% of the frame Eyes are open and clearly visible No glasses, headwear, or heavy photo filters Photo was taken within the last 6 months Taking two minutes to verify each of these points before submitting can save you days of delays. Conclusion A rejected photo is one of the easiest problems to avoid when applying for a Thai e-Visa and one of the most frustrating when it happens. By following the official photo specifications outlined in this guide, you can submit your application with confidence. Foreign workers in Saudi Arabia must hold a valid work and residence permit (Iqama) to work legally in the country. Table of contents What is the Saudi Arabia work permit for Who’s eligible for a Saudi Arabia work permit Documents needed to apply for a Saudi Arabia work permit (Iqama) Iqama photo requirements Get a photo for a Saudi Arabia work permit online! Iqama rules in Saudi Arabia The Iqama proves your right to reside and work in Saudi Arabia legally. If a foreign worker does not have a work visa, they may have to pay a fine of SAR 10,000 and are also likely to face arrest and deportation. Iqama also serves as the primary ID type for foreigners in Saudi Arabia. It is desirable to have it with you at all times to always be ready to prove your legal status. Remember that if you temporarily leave Saudi Arabia during your work contract, you must apply for additional exit and re-entry permits. Work permit requirements for Saudi Arabia If you have a job offer lined in in Saudi Arabia, offered by an employer based in the country, count yourself eligible. In addition, you must be over the age of 21. You must also undergo a medical examination at an accredited centre for dangerous diseases. It is important that you do not have a criminal record. As a rule, the hiring company must first be approved since there are quotas for the number of foreign workers in Saudi Arabia. The quotas depend on the profession, age and nationality of the employees. While the employer is the one who applies, your documents are ultimately your own and you should have them ready for application. You also must undergo a medical examination for dangerous diseases at an accredited centre. How to apply for a Saudi work visa? If you have successfully concluded a contract with a Saudi employer, congratulations - you have done most of the job. Then, your employer has to start an application process on your behalf. After you arrive in Saudi Arabia with the work visa, your employer will have to apply for your residence permit, including the work permit. The Iqama application must be started within 90 days after your arrival. Your employer must cover all the fees. While the employer is the one who applies, your documents are ultimately your own, and you should have them ready for application. Documents needed to apply for a Saudi Arabia work visa The paperwork you will need to prepare are as follows: Your valid passport; Two photographs of yourself that fulfill requirements; A letter from your employer/visa sponsor, certified by the Chamber of Commerce as well as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; A signed employment contract; Certificates of academic and professional qualifications; A police report detailing any convictions. As a rule, there shouldn’t be any, and this report is supposed to prove it as is needed; A medical report from a licensed physician. Iqama photo requirements Make sure the photographs you use to apply satisfy the following parameters: The photo must be in color; The photo size must be 40 mm in width and 60 mm in height; The height of your head in the picture should range at 85% of the overall photo height; The photo must be no older than six months; The background must be plain white; Glasses are allowed. The frame must not cover any part of your eyes. There must be no glare on the lenses. Dark glasses are not permitted; You can wear a head covering for religious or medical reasons. Your full facial features must be visible. You cannot wear head accessories for any other reason; Your photo must be in focus. Balance the lighting and colour, not too dark or too light; There must not be any shadows on your face or behind your head; 'Red eye' in photographs is not acceptable; Keep your facial expression neutral and look straight into the camera. No additional documentation is required on your part. How much does the Iqama application cost? The Saudi work visa applications must be paid by the employer. Rates depend on the percentage of Saudi nationals in the hiring company. If more than 50% of employees are Saudi nationals, the overall fee will be SAR 7,200 (almost $2000). Meeting our photo standards The photo you give us for your visa application or NZeTA request must: clearly identify you not be altered, and meet our photo standards. Your photo will be collected and used as biometric information to: establish a record of your identity establish or verify your identity, and assist in making a decision on your visa application. Meeting our photo standards If your photo does not meet our standards, for example does not clearly show your face, your application will take longer. We may ask you for a new photo. Pro viding a photo that meets our requirements is required for visa applications and NZeTA requests and authorised by the Immigration Act 2009 and the Immigration Regulations made under that Act . If you do not pro vide a photo , we may not be able to accept, or pro cess your visa application or NZeTA request, or we may decline your application or refuse your request. Errors and common mistakes If there is a problem with your photo you will get an error message when you submit your visa or NZeTA photo with your online application. Fixing errors when uploading a photo Photo standards To meet our legal and technical standards, your photo must meet a number of specifications. Your photo must: look like you have been taken within the last 6 months be a photo of you which is not edited or altered, and not be a photo of a photo. Photos that are AI enhanced or altered do not meet our standards. If you use AI to edit your photos your visa application or NZeTA request will be delayed or could be declined. Photos for online applications Size and format the photo correctly Your photo must be: between 512 KB and 3.14 MB taken in portrait mode with 3:4 aspect ratio a JPG or JPEG file. Example: This photo shows acceptable visa photo dimensions. Do not edit or enhance the photo The photo must be natural and unaltered. Do not use: filters beautification features AI editing tools. This includes: changing the colour, brightness, contrast or sharpness cropping your head and shoulders to place it on a plain background changing your facial features, for example, size, shape or colour of your eyes, nose, ears, mouth, cheekbones, or eyebrows skin smoothing or face slimming digitally removing objects from the photo, especially around the image of your face, for example, glasses, jewellery, headbands, hats or toys on or around the image. Note If your phone automatically filters or alters photos when you take them, turn this feature off when taking your visa or NZeTA photo. Examples: The person in the photo on the left has not been altered to change the lighting, focus or contrast (correct). The photo on the right has been digitally altered to change the person's eye size, lips and slim their face (incorrect). Position your face correctly Make sure: your face covers between 70% and 80% of the image and is in the middle of the frame you are looking straight at the camera with a neutral expression and your mouth is closed, and your face is not turned to the side or on an angle. Examples: The photo on the left shows a person looking directly at the camera with their head straight-on (correct). The photo on the right shows a person looking off to the right with their head turned (incorrect). Be clearly visible Make sure the photo clearly shows your facial features. Your hair must not cover your face or ears — the photo must show your ears unless you wear a scarf for religious or medical reasons. Remove any head coverings (unless worn for religious or medical reasons). If you wear a head covering for religious or medical reasons, your covering must not cover your mouth or the sides of your face. Your eyes must be open. The image must be in focus and not blurry. Examples: The person in the photo on the left has their eyes open and mouth shut (correct). The person in the photo on the right has their mouth open and their expression is not neutral (incorrect). The photo on the left is in focus (correct). The photo on the right is blurry (incorrect). The person on the left is an example of how to wear a head covering correctly for your photo. The person in the photo on the right has a covering that covers their mouth and the sides of their face (incorrect). If you wear glasses You can wear prescription glasses. Make sure your glasses: are clear and not tinted — no sunglasses do not have heavy frames that cover your face, and do not create a glare or reflection in the photo. If you are having issues with glasses, it may be best to remove them for your photo. The photo on the left shows a person wearing thin rimmed glasses with no glare that do not obscure the face (correct). The photo on the right shows a person wearing thick rimmed dark glasses that obscure the face (incorrect). Use good lighting Your photo must: have no shadows on your face or the background. have good contrast between your face and the background. To create good lighting: stand 0.5 metres from the background, and the photographer must be 1.5 metres in front of you when they take the photo. Examples: The photo on the left is an example of good lighting. The lighting in the photo on the right is too dark. Use a plain background Objects in the background of your photo may prevent our system from recognising your face. The background of your photo must: be neutral and plain, and only show you and no other people or objects. Avoid wearing t-shirts with pictures on them, flowery or patterned backgrounds and clothing. Patterns can create technical issues with our system. Examples: The photo on the left has a plain background (correct). The photo on the right has a objects in the background (incorrect). Using selfies It can be difficult to take a selfie that meets our photo requirements. Where possible, we recommend that you have someone else take your photo, to our requirements. You can only use a selfie photo if you use the mobile app to apply for an NZeTA. If you are applying in the mobile app and you only have the option of submitting a selfie, make sure: your arm is stretched out as far as possible to create space between the phone and your face you hold the phone at the same height as your eyebrows the light source is behind the phone or camera. Examples: The photo on the left is correct (not a selfie). The other photo is a selfie and incorrect because of the background, positioning, and lighting. Photos for paper-based visa applications The photo you submit with a paper application must be 35 mm wide and 45 mm high. More instructions are on the paper application forms. Note You can only apply for an NZeTA online. Using a professional photographer We are more likely to accept your photo if you use a professional photographer. Make sure: the photographer has our requirements the photo file size is less than 10 MB. Taking acceptable visa photos (pdf, 364 KB) Taking acceptable visa photos in Simplified Chinese (pdf, 1.2 MB) How we collect, use and store your photo Check our privacy statement and our ‘Collecting and using biometric information’ page for more about how we collect, use, store, disclose, retain, and protect biometric information like photos. There is also information about your rights to request access to or correct your information and how to make a complaint, including complaining to the Privacy Commissioner. https://www.isic.lt/en/requirements-for-.text: EN LT EN ISIC Blog Discounts Discounts in Lithuania Discounts abroad Public transport discounts ISIC App and Virtual ID ISIC Card About ISIC card Popular questions ISIC App and Virtual ID ISIC Global Cooperation Order ISIC Contacts Order ISIC ISIC Blog Discounts Discounts in Lithuania Discounts abroad Public transport discounts ISIC App and Virtual ID ISIC Card About ISIC card Popular questions ISIC App and Virtual ID ISIC Global Cooperation Order ISIC Contacts Requirements for a photo Photo specifications for the ISIC/ITIC card must comply to the following specifications: A passport-style photograph (i.e. headshot only); Only the cardholder is visible in the photograph; The photograph must be clear, well defined and taken against a plain white or light-coloured background; A recent photograph (i.e. taken in the last 6 months); Face must not be covered and looking square to the camera; Glasses are acceptable, as long as the eyes are clearly visible. Make sure that the frame does not cover any part of the eyes. Sunglasses are not acceptable; A hairpiece or other cosmetic accessory is acceptable if it does not disguise cardholder’s normal appearance; Cardholders wearing a head covering for religious reasons, must make sure full facial features are not obscured. Please note: If the photographs do not meet the required specifications, they will be rejected and this will cause a delay in the card’s activation.
